items.title: Hello, World!
Variables and Data Types
items.content:
## Variables and Data Types

Java is **statically typed**: every variable has a type known at compile time.

```java
int age = 21;
double pi = 3.14;
String name = "Ada";
boolean isActive = true;
char letter = 'A';
```

### Primitive types

| Type     | Size    | Values                        |
|----------|---------|-------------------------------|
| `byte`   | 1 byte  | -128 to 127                   |
| `short`  | 2 bytes | -32768 to 32767               |
| `int`    | 4 bytes | -2^31 to 2^31-1               |
| `long`   | 8 bytes | -2^63 to 2^63-1 (suffix `L`)  |
| `float`  | 4 bytes | ~7 decimal digits (suffix `f`)|
| `double` | 8 bytes | ~15 decimal digits            |
| `char`   | 2 bytes | A Unicode character           |
| `boolean`| 1 bit   | `true` / `false`              |

### Reference types

Everything else — `String`, arrays, objects — is a **reference type** that points to an object on the heap.

### Declaring variables

```java
int x;          // declaration
x = 10;         // assignment
int y = 20;     // declaration + initialisation
final double TAX_RATE = 0.08;   // constant, cannot be reassigned
```

### Naming conventions

- Classes: `PascalCase` (`Student`, `HttpClient`).
- Variables and methods: `camelCase` (`userName`, `calculateTotal`).
- Constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` (`MAX_SIZE`).

### Arithmetic

```java
int a = 10, b = 3;
int sum = a + b;       // 13
int diff = a - b;      // 7
int prod = a * b;      // 30
int quot = a / b;      // 3  (integer division)
int rem = a % b;       // 1
double dq = (double) a / b;  // 3.333...  (cast first)
```

### String concatenation

```java
String greeting = "Hello, " + name + "!";
System.out.println("age is " + age);   // number auto-converts
```

---

**Next up:** reading input with the Scanner.

items.title: Reading Input with Scanner
Operators and Type Conversion
items.content:
## Operators and Type Conversion

### Increment and decrement

```java
int n = 5;
n++;          // n == 6
++n;          // n == 7
int a = 5;
int b = a++;  // b == 5, a == 6 (post-increment returns old value)
int c = ++a;  // a == 7, c == 7 (pre-increment returns new value)
```

### Compound assignment

```java
x += 5;   // x = x + 5
x -= 2;   // x = x - 2
x *= 3;
x /= 4;
x %= 2;
```

### Relational and logical operators

```java
==   !=   <   >   <=   >=
&&   ||   !
```

### Type conversion

**Widening** (implicit) happens when converting to a larger type:

```java
int i = 42;
long l = i;          // int -> long (safe, automatic)
double d = i;        // int -> double (safe, automatic)
```

**Narrowing** (explicit) requires a cast and can lose data:

```java
double d = 3.99;
int i = (int) d;     // 3  — truncates the fraction
```

### The ternary operator

```java
int max = (a > b) ? a : b;
```

### String to number

```java
int n = Integer.parseInt("42");      // 42
double d = Double.parseDouble("3.14");
long l = Long.parseLong("123456789");
```

### The Math class

```java
Math.max(a, b);
Math.min(a, b);
Math.abs(x);
Math.pow(2, 10);      // 1024.0
Math.sqrt(81);        // 9.0
Math.round(3.6);      // 4 (long)
```

---

items.title: Strings and StringBuilder
items.content:
## Strings and StringBuilder

### Strings are immutable

Every `String` operation that "changes" the string creates a new object.

```java
String s = "hello";
String t = s.toUpperCase();   // "HELLO"; s unchanged
```

### Common String methods

| Method              | Purpose                     |
|---------------------|-----------------------------|
| `length()`          | Number of characters        |
| `charAt(i)`         | Character at index `i`      |
| `substring(a,b)`    | Slice `[a, b)`              |
| `indexOf(ch)`       | First index or `-1`         |
| `startsWith(x)`     | Prefix check                |
| `endsWith(x)`       | Suffix check                |
| `contains(x)`       | Substring check             |
| `replace(a,b)`      | Replace all `a` with `b`    |
| `split(regex)`      | Split into `String[]`       |
| `trim()`            | Strip surrounding whitespace|
| `toLowerCase()`     | Lowercase                   |
| `equals(other)`     | **Content** comparison      |
| `equalsIgnoreCase`  | Case-insensitive compare    |

### equals, not ==

`==` compares references; `equals` compares content:

```java
String a = new String("hi");
String b = new String("hi");
a == b;             // false (different objects)
a.equals(b);        // true (same content)
```

### StringBuilder

Concatenating in a loop creates many throwaway strings. `StringBuilder` is mutable and efficient:

```java
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    sb.append(i).append(" ");
}
String result = sb.toString();   // "0 1 2 3 4 "
```

### Reverse a string

```java
String reversed = new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString();
```

---

**Next up:** ArrayList and generics.

items.title: ArrayList and Generics
items.content:
## ArrayList and Generics

`ArrayList` is a resizable array from the Collections Framework.

### Creating an ArrayList

```java
import java.util.ArrayList;

ArrayList<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
ArrayList<Integer> numbers = new ArrayList<>();   // wrapper type, not int
```

### Common methods

| Method              | Purpose                     |
|---------------------|-----------------------------|
| `add(x)`            | Append                      |
| `add(index, x)`     | Insert at index             |
| `get(index)`        | Read                        |
| `set(index, x)`     | Replace                     |
| `remove(index)`     | Remove by index             |
| `remove(obj)`       | Remove first match          |
| `size()`            | Element count               |
| `contains(x)`       | Membership check            |
| `indexOf(x)`        | First index or `-1`         |
| `clear()`           | Remove all                  |
| `isEmpty()`         | Is it empty?                |

### Iterating

```java
for (int i = 0; i < numbers.size(); i++) {
    System.out.println(numbers.get(i));
}

for (int n : numbers) {
    System.out.println(n);
}
```

### Autoboxing

Java automatically converts between primitives and wrappers:

```java
ArrayList<Integer> list = new ArrayList<>();
list.add(42);              // int -> Integer (autoboxing)
int x = list.get(0);       // Integer -> int (unboxing)
```

### Generics

The `<Integer>` syntax is a **generic** type parameter. It tells the compiler the element type, so mistakes fail at compile time instead of runtime.

### The diamond operator

```java
ArrayList<String> list = new ArrayList<>();   // <> infers the type
```

---

**Next up:** HashMap and other collections.

Lambdas and Functional Interfaces
items.content:
## Lambdas and Functional Interfaces

A **lambda** is a compact way to implement a functional interface — an interface with a single abstract method.

### A functional interface

```java
interface Greeter {
    String greet(String name);
}
```

### Lambda syntax

```java
Greeter g = name -> "Hello, " + name;
System.out.println(g.greet("Ada"));   // Hello, Ada
```

Lambda forms:

```java
() -> 42                        // no parameters
x -> x * 2                      // one parameter
(int a, int b) -> a + b         // explicit types
(s1, s2) -> s1.length() - s2.length()   // inferred types
```

### Passing behavior as data

```java
interface Calculator {
    int apply(int a, int b);
}

int operate(Calculator c, int a, int b) {
    return c.apply(a, b);
}

operate((a, b) -> a + b, 3, 4);    // 7
operate((a, b) -> a * b, 3, 4);    // 12
```

### Common functional interfaces

| Interface       | Method         | Use                   |
|-----------------|----------------|-----------------------|
| `Runnable`      | `run()`        | Side effects          |
| `Supplier<T>`   | `get()`        | Provide a value       |
| `Consumer<T>`   | `accept(t)`    | Consume a value       |
| `Function<T,R>` | `apply(t)`     | Transform             |
| `Predicate<T>`  | `test(t)`      | Return boolean        |
| `Comparator<T>` | `compare(a,b)` | Ordering              |

### Comparator with a lambda

```java
List<String> names = new ArrayList<>(List.of("Bob", "Ada", "Zoe"));
names.sort((a, b) -> a.length() - b.length());
```

---

**Next up:** the Stream API.

items.title: The Stream API
items.content:
## The Stream API

Streams process collections declaratively with a pipeline of operations.

### Basic pipeline

```java
List<Integer> numbers = List.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);

List<Integer> evensSquared =
    numbers.stream()
           .filter(n -> n % 2 == 0)   // intermediate
           .map(n -> n * n)           // intermediate
           .toList();                 // terminal
```

### Common operations

| Operation         | Kind         | Purpose                  |
|-------------------|--------------|--------------------------|
| `filter(p)`       | intermediate | Keep matching items      |
| `map(f)`          | intermediate | Transform each item      |
| `sorted()`        | intermediate | Sort                     |
| `distinct()`      | intermediate | Remove duplicates        |
| `limit(n)`        | intermediate | Take first n             |
| `skip(n)`         | intermediate | Drop first n             |
| `collect(...)`    | terminal     | Gather into a collection |
| `toList()`        | terminal     | Into a list (Java 16+)   |
| `count()`         | terminal     | Count items              |
| `anyMatch(p)`     | terminal     | Any match?               |
| `allMatch(p)`     | terminal     | All match?               |
| `reduce(init, f)` | terminal     | Fold                     |

### Examples

```java
long count = numbers.stream().filter(n -> n > 3).count();

boolean anyEven = numbers.stream().anyMatch(n -> n % 2 == 0);

int sum = numbers.stream().reduce(0, Integer::sum);

numbers.stream().sorted().forEach(System.out::println);
```

### Method references

```java
numbers.stream().map(String::valueOf).toList();   // int -> "1", "2", ...
names.sort(String::compareTo);
```

---

**Next up:** file, generics, and lambda exercises.
